reasons.text: Buys feedstock inside a closed loop of 3 recyclers trading the same material (95% of its feedstock)
Electricity bought is only 0.20x the minimum needed for the tonnes claimed (59 kWh/t against at least 300)
Sold products equal only 3% of the output expected from the tonnes claimed
100% of certificate tonnes were sold below the cost of recycling (average 0.20x the cost floor)
25% of purchase invoices have suspiciously round tonnages (typical plant: about 2%)
Declared capacity of 11,930 t/yr needs about 2.2x the power the plant is connected for

inspection_checklist: Trace the material flow between the plants in the loop (weighbridge slips, vehicle GPS); the same tonnes may be invoiced round a ring.
Obtain the DISCOM consumption statement and meter readings for the flagged months; compare connected machinery (kW) against the claimed tonnage.
Reconcile product sales with processed tonnes; contact the product buyers listed and verify that they received the material.
Ask for the plant's cost sheet; certificates priced below the cost of recycling imply the processing cost was never incurred.
Physically verify a sample of purchase invoices with the sellers (weighbridge slips, e-way bills, vehicle logs).
